items.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023
items.q: I did, I wrote “Singing the Blues” after I went to see Bobby “Blue” Bland play... I got that idea from listening to Bobby “Blue” Bland and his horns

ctx.x: I am so totally fascinated how the 12-bar blues has provided a template for thousands of songs of every topic, every groove. It’s just the most elegant song form that I can ever think about.

It’s very true. I think that’s why I tend to stay in and around blues. Because there’s so much to experiment with it. And I do a lot of — I know I’m known as a blues singer and I do a lot of these, I do these cruises. And it gives me a chance to hear all different types of blues. And that keeps me going too. It gives me a lot of ideas. And a lot of my blues is mixed with other genres too. It’s got a little bit of reggae in some of them, in some of the songs that I do I mix a little bit of that Bobby “Blue” Bland…

I saw the — the first time I saw a blues cruise advertised I had to chuckle because how can you possibly have the blues when you’re on a cruise? But then I see you wrote “Singing the Blues” on a cruise, is that right? Staring at the mirror/Singing the blues.
